description: WebAuthn passkeys are a first-class credential and second factor.

requirements.description: Users must be able to register WebAuthn passkeys as either a primary passwordless credential or a second factor. The service implements the WebAuthn relying party role: generating and validating registration and authentication ceremonies. Registered authenticators are stored in SQLite (credential ID, public key, sign count, AAGUID). Sign-count validation must detect cloned authenticators. Passkey operations are audited.
requirements.deferred_reason: WebAuthn is not required for the owner-to-principal delegation path and is deliberately outside this delivery.
requirements.revisit_trigger: Passwordless browser sign-in or phishing-resistant second-factor support becomes an active product requirement.
requirements.title: Passkeys / WebAuthn as First-Class Credential and Second Factor

validation.notes: api/internal/webauthn/webauthn_test.go: generate registration challenge, simulate valid authenticator response (using a software authenticator), verify credential stored with correct sign count
api/internal/webauthn/webauthn_test.go: replay an authentication response with a stale sign count → rejected as potential cloned authenticator
api/internal/webauthn/webauthn_test.go: tampered clientDataJSON or authData fails attestation verification
api/handlers/webauthn/webauthn_e2e_test.go: register passkey for a user using a software authenticator library; sign in using the passkey → session issued
api/handlers/webauthn/webauthn_e2e_test.go: passkey used as second factor after password — password step succeeds, then WebAuthn challenge must be satisfied before session is issued
bas/mfa/passkey_enrollment_test: user navigates to security settings, registers a passkey using the browser WebAuthn API (simulated), signs out, and signs back in using the passkey without a password

title: Passkeys / WebAuthn
